title: delayAsymmetry management input, timestamp-calibration triple, and the live UART tuner from the prototype line
body:
The current tree has no delayAsymmetry anywhere (`git grep -i asym` is empty), no ingress/egress-latency calibration at the bench timestamp latches, and no way to adjust any of the three against a wire reference without a full rebuild. The prototype line (tag `prototype-line`) had all three: `cfg_asym_i` as a 64-bit management input applied per 802.1AS-2011 11.2.15 in the pdelay/offset arithmetic, ingressLatency subtracted at the RX latch and egressLatency added at the TX latch per 8.4.3 timestamp-point compensation, and `bench_uart_tune.sv`, a 115200-8N1 RX-only tuner (Y/I/E hex commands) so the triple could be adjusted live instead of a 13-minute rebuild per value - the mechanism behind the prototype's TAP-calibrated lock record.

Porting is a real feature lane, not a cherry-pick: the input must enter the ucode-v7 gather faces and the current offset arithmetic, the bench latches must grow the compensation points, and the verification bar owes arms for asymmetry-applied offset and for the latch compensation on both faces. The strict-threshold hardware record (800 ns neighborPropDelayThresh with no profile deviations) depended on this calibration; without it the bench measures the raw MAC latencies.

The verification-layer half of the prototype replay landed in #56 and the documentation record is #57; this is the third and last unported piece.
